REGISTERED ESTABLISHMENT
EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
1. Establishment Details
2. Registered Export Operations

This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for organic wheat (grain). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
3. Registration Status

Registration RE-VIC-2023-0055 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 7 July 2023 and the current registration period extends to 6 July 2026. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person

Helena Marinos is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2021. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description

The registered premises comprise Lot 42 on Plan DP 791144, located at 55 Western Highway, Stawell VIC 3380. The total registered area is 5.3 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
6.2 Services and Utilities
6.3 Adjoining Sites

The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow

A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: organic wheat is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities

The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of organic wheat. Total storage capacity is approximately 1,200 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes

No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises

No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

13. Food Safety Program

A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping

Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No site-specific hygiene and sanitation program documented for Geraldton Fish & Grain Markets Pty Ltd. General industry practices are referenced but no cleaning schedules, chemicals, personnel hygiene procedures or records are defined.

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
Waste management procedures for Geraldton Fish & Grain Markets Pty Ltd are NOT included in this HACCP plan. No waste streams, disposal methods, frequencies or records are documented.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT SITE-SPECIFIC / EFFECTIVENESS NOT DEMONSTRATED]
The HACCP plan mentions 'bait stations in storage' (CCP for rodents rated non-CCP, Risk=4) but does not include a formal pest control program for the Kununurra gin facility.

Missing:
• No site-specific pest control program (no bait station map, no monitoring schedule).
• No pest control contractor engaged or documented.
• No monitoring frequency specified.
• No corrective action procedure if infestation detected.
• No records of past pest control activities.

Pest effectiveness CANNOT be demonstrated without a documented, implemented program.

ACTION REQUIRED: Develop and implement a site-specific Pest Control Program including:
(a) Bait station map with station IDs; (b) Inspection frequency (minimum monthly);
(c) Insect pitfall traps in storage; (d) Licensed pest contractor engagement;
(e) Corrective action procedures; (f) Records retention minimum 2 years.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No documented traceability system linking receival, processing, packing and dispatch for Geraldton Fish & Grain Markets Pty Ltd. No lot coding, one-step-back/forward procedures, or recall protocol.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No formal failed goods procedure for Geraldton Fish & Grain Markets Pty Ltd. No documented process for segregation, re-testing, downgrade, destruction or DAFF notification.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)

Phytosanitary Security (KCG-PSP-001):
• Fumigated export bales stored in sealed shed area; access restricted.
• Bale identification: each bale stencilled with bale number, gin ID and destination.
• Container inspection before loading; seal number recorded on dispatch docket.
• DAFF sampling and phytosanitary certificate issued per consignment.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. OVERVIEW

Grampians Organic Wheat is a registered export establishment located at 55 Western Highway, Stawell VIC 3380, VIC. The establishment holds RE Number RE-VIC-2023-0055 and is registered to handle and export Lupins under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
3. EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
4. FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1 Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)

The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Lupins.
4.2 Lighting (C2)

High-efficiency LED battens throughout: 470 lux packing hall, 360 lux cool store entry, 342 lux dispatch bay. Sensor-activated step-lighting along conveyor access walkways. All fittings shatterproof-sleeved, IP54 rated minimum.
4.3 Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)

Purpose-built amenities: 1 toilet, 2 hand basins — insulated hot-water system, soap and single-use paper towels. Amenities connected to main processing building via covered walkway. In-line handwash basin at processing floor entry point.
5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1 Cleanability (C4)

Purpose-built construction with cleanability designed in: coved epoxy floors, smooth coated-steel wall panels, no horizontal ledges on equipment or structure, all joints sealed with food-grade silicone, recessed floor drain channels with removable SS covers. Annual deep-clean by specialist contractor supplements weekly programme.
5.2 Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

Building envelope sealed to export standard: galvanised mesh (6 mm) on all openings; door brush seals replaced every 2 years; expansion joints filled with flexible polyurethane; no open eaves — soffit board sealed to top of wall cladding; all roof penetrations (vents, conduits) flashed and sealed. No horizontal structural members without drainage slope.
5.3 Waste Disposal Design (C6)

Waste disposal: bunded concrete waste pad (4×6 m, 150 mm kerb on 3 sides) adjacent to building for solid waste collection in sealed lidded bins; liquid waste to licensed grease-trap and sewer connection; dust collection by wet scrubber — effluent to contained holding pond; all chemical waste in labelled containers in chemical store for licensed disposal. Records maintained.
6. VICSTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1 Waste Management Procedures (C7)

Waste Management SOP (WM-SOP-179, version 2.4, current): specifies waste stream segregation, bin placement, collection frequencies and disposal methods. Reviewed bi-annually. Non-conformances logged in the corrective action register. Accessible to all staff on site intranet.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1 Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)

Internal inspection results: floor — no accumulated debris in corners or wall bases; equipment — all conveyor belts, rollers and hoppers clean; overhead structure — free from hanging debris; drains — clear and odour-free; amenities — clean with full consumable stocks. Last full deep-clean: 6 weeks prior to this assessment.
7.2 Pest Condition (C9)

Current pest status: all monitoring indicators within acceptable range. Rodent bait consumption at routine background level. Insect sticky traps show no grain storage pest species. No evidence of bird entry. Bait station register up to date and signed by licensed pest management technician (last service: February 2025).

HYGIENE & VICNITATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
2. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment
This plan covers the processing and storage areas of the establishment. Loading and dispatch dock operations are covered separately under the Export Logistics Procedure.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Wheat during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3. PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
4. MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
5. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival Pit / Weighbridge

Pre-receival: Inspect pit and scale platform for residual grain from previous lot. Activate compressed air lance to dislodge grain from crevices, joints and conveyor housings. Sweep accumulated grain into collection bin. Wipe scale display and control panel with damp cloth. Supervisor to sign pre-loading checklist before grain intake commences.
Elevator Boot & Leg Casings

At end of each operating day: Lock out elevator drive before opening access hatch. Using industrial vacuum, extract all dead-stock grain from boot throat, casing joints, and transition points. Inspect internal surfaces for grain bridges or insect webbing. Record any pest signs in the Pest Monitoring Log. Replace and secure access hatch. Enter completed task in Equipment Cleaning Log.
Belt Conveyors & Augers

Weekly maintenance cleaning: Isolate drive motor and lock out before commencing. Run conveyor empty for five minutes to clear carrying strand. Remove belt guards and clean all carry rollers and return rollers with a stiff brush. Vacuum accumulated grain and dust from trough pan. Inspect belt splice and edges for wear. Reassemble all guards before returning to service. Record in Cleaning Log.
Grain Storage Silos / Bins

Between commodity lots: Full physical inspection and clean-out required before loading a new grain lot. Access silo through roof hatch or side door (confined space procedure applies). Sweep-out all surfaces using long-handled broom. Vacuum residue from cone and floor. Inspect walls and roof for webbing, insect activity, or mould. Record findings on Pre-Loading Checklist. Silo must not be loaded until the checklist is signed by the Storage Manager.
Grain Screening / Cleaning Plant

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Grain Screening / Cleaning Plant in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6. MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES

Particular attention is given to dead-stock zones in elevator boots, conveyor transition points, and auger troughs. These areas accumulate grain that cannot self-clear during normal operation and provide harbouring conditions for stored product insects. Full physical extraction is required at each lot change.
7. APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
8. RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1 Record System

Cleaning records are maintained using a combination of paper log sheets and digital entries in the site management system. All records are retained at site for a minimum of two years from the date of completion.
8.2 Sanitation Verification Log Template
9. VERIFICATION PROCEDURES

ATP (adenosine triphosphate) swab testing is used monthly on critical food-contact surfaces to verify cleaning efficacy. Results are recorded in the Surface Hygiene Register alongside the cleaning log.
10. NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION

Any area found to be in an unacceptable hygiene condition is withdrawn from service. Cleaning is repeated and verified before re-use. All corrective actions are documented and reviewed at the monthly management meeting.
11. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)

The most recent quarterly hygiene review at Grampians Organic Wheat (conducted 15 April 2025) confirmed that all areas are maintained in accordance with this Hygiene and Sanitation Plan. No corrective actions outstanding.
